# Modules whose version changes make a PR Tier 1 (#3389).
#
# `tier1-review` takes its Tier 1 floor from the CODEOWNERS paths a PR touches,
# but a dependency manifest is the wrong granularity for that rule. Every Go
# bump touches `go.mod`, so owning the file made every bump Tier 1 and put the
# whole dependency queue behind a human sign-off. The module is the right
# granularity: a change to a `go.mod` or `go.sum` anywhere in the repository is
# Tier 1 only when it moves one of the modules below. Every other path still
# takes its tier from CODEOWNERS, and `/go.mod` stays there as the ownership
# record.
#
# A dependency bump genuinely can be a data-path change: #3208 was a
# conduit-connector-sdk bump whose entire purpose was fixing a source `Run`
# `tomb.Go` race. The test for a line here is whether a wrong version of the
# module could drop, duplicate, reorder or corrupt a record, or change a
# serialized format.
#
# One module path per line; `#` starts a comment. A line matches that module and
# everything under it, so `github.com/conduitio/conduit-commons` covers
# `.../conduit-commons/v2` and `.../conduit-commons/paramgen`; major-version
# suffixes need no separate line.
#
# What the gate treats as Tier 1 without consulting this list: a change to the
# `go`, `toolchain` or `module` directive, a manifest whose diff the API did not
# return, and any manifest line the parser cannot classify. It fails closed, so
# an unreadable or unwired list makes every bump Tier 1 rather than none of
# them. See .github/scripts/tier1_review.py.
#
# Adding a line is cheap. Removing one is weakening a gate, and this file lives
# under /.github/, which DeVaris owns.

# The engine's own contracts: records, positions, the plugin protocol, the SDKs.
github.com/conduitio/conduit-commons
github.com/conduitio/conduit-connector-protocol
github.com/conduitio/conduit-connector-sdk
github.com/conduitio/conduit-processor-sdk

# Built-in connectors. Records flow through these inside the shipped binary.
github.com/conduitio/conduit-connector-file
github.com/conduitio/conduit-connector-generator
github.com/conduitio/conduit-connector-kafka
github.com/conduitio/conduit-connector-log
github.com/conduitio/conduit-connector-postgres
github.com/conduitio/conduit-connector-s3

# Schema and serialization: the wire formats and the registry client.
github.com/conduitio/conduit-schema-registry
github.com/iskorotkov/avro
github.com/hamba/avro
github.com/twmb/franz-go

# Serialized state. goccy/go-json encodes the store entries (pkg/pipeline/store.go
# and its neighbours); badger is the embedded KV store's on-disk format.
github.com/goccy/go-json
github.com/dgraph-io/badger

# Pipeline configuration is a public contract and this parser defines it.
github.com/conduitio/yaml
